status_summary: No transfer of VAERS, the Vaccine Safety Datalink or CISA to FDA, and no statute or regulation barring prescriptive CDC guidance, was found as of 2026-10-08; VAERS is already run jointly by FDA and CDC. HHS instead changed the recommendations themselves, a step in the same direction as the Mandate's preference for leaving more choices to parents and clinicians but with a different design: the Secretary removed all 17 ACIP members on 2025-06-09, ACIP voted on 2025-12-05 for individual-based decision-making on the hepatitis B birth dose for infants of mothers who test negative, and an HHS decision memo dated 2026-01-05 cut the routinely recommended childhood schedule from 17 diseases to 11 (per KFF). What is stopped: on 2026-03-16 Judge Brian Murphy (D. Mass., American Academy of Pediatrics v. Kennedy, No. 1:25-cv-11916) issued an order that the parties' filings call a stay and preliminary relief (some press accounts call it a preliminary injunction; the legal basis was not stated in the sources read). According to the plaintiffs' First Circuit filing, it stayed the CDC's 2026-01-05 decision memo, the appointments of thirteen ACIP members (appointed 2025-06-11, 2025-09-11 and 2026-01-13) and all votes of ACIP as so composed; a Georgetown Center on Children and Families summary lists the stayed votes as the June 2025 thimerosal vote, the September 2025 COVID-19 vote and the December 2025 hepatitis B vote. What is not stopped: the pre-2026-01-05 schedule stays in force, the order does not bar a lawfully constituted ACIP from meeting, and the same Georgetown summary says the court granted no preliminary relief against the May 2025 Secretary directive on COVID-19 vaccination for healthy children and pregnant women. HHS filed its notice of appeal on 2026-04-29 (First Circuit No. 26-1503); the plaintiffs' 2026-06-15 filing says the government appealed only the stay of the thirteen appointments and not the stays of the schedule memo or the votes, the defendants describe the appeal as concerning preliminary relief on the Federal Advisory Committee Act claim, and a Courthouse News report of the argument says the Justice Department asked the panel to vacate the stay; the exact scope of the appeal is therefore not settled in the sources read. The panel (Judges Barron, Dunlap and Kayatta) heard argument on 2026-10-06 and gave no indication of when it would rule. The district court paused its proceedings pending the appeal on 2026-07-23, and on 2026-09-03 the defendants asked to extend that pause to three weeks after the First Circuit's opinion, stating that the 2026-03-16 order remains in place; a ruling on that request was not found. Executive Order 14407 (2026-05-29) and Executive Order 14420 (signed 2026-08-10, 91 FR 53173) address recommendations by executive order; EO 14420 sets three recommendation categories, directs the Task Force on Safer Childhood Vaccines to present plans within 90 days (including on improving vaccine safety monitoring) and directs the Attorney General to support challenges to conflicting state laws. Neither order mentions VAERS, the Vaccine Safety Datalink or FDA.

timeline.event: HHS announces the Secretary has removed all 17 sitting members of ACIP.

ACIP votes 8 to 3 to recommend individual-based (shared clinical) decision-making on the hepatitis B vaccine for infants born to mothers who test negative, including the birth dose; a first dose for infants without the birth dose is suggested no earlier than two months.

An HHS decision memo revises the childhood and adolescent schedule, reducing routinely recommended diseases from 17 to 11 and moving several to shared clinical decision-making (the memo PDF could not be read; reported by KFF).

Judge Brian Murphy (D. Mass.), in a suit by medical organizations (American Academy of Pediatrics v. Kennedy, No. 1:25-cv-11916), stays the CDC's 2026-01-05 schedule memo, the appointments of thirteen ACIP members and all votes of ACIP as so composed, on the ground that the 2025 replacement of the committee did not follow Federal Advisory Committee Act requirements (as reported by Pharmaceutical Executive citing NPR and IDSA, and described in the plaintiffs' First Circuit filing). The pre-2026 schedule remains in force and the order does not bar a lawfully constituted ACIP. HHS appeals on 2026-04-29 (First Circuit No. 26-1503).

Executive Order 14407 (Realigning United States Core Childhood Vaccine Recommendations with Best Practices from Peer, Developed Countries) is signed; it directs a review and update of the childhood schedule and alignment of agencies with it, and does not mention FDA, VAERS or the Vaccine Safety Datalink.

The district court grants the defendants' renewed motion to pause further proceedings pending the expedited First Circuit appeal of the preliminary relief on the Federal Advisory Committee Act claim (ECF 347). A defendants' motion filed 2026-09-03 asks to extend the pause to three weeks after the First Circuit opinion, states that the 2026-03-16 order remains in place to protect the plaintiffs, and says the First Circuit set argument for 2026-10-06.

Executive Order 14420 is signed (published 2026-08-14, 91 FR 53173): three recommendation categories (all children, high-risk groups, shared clinical decision-making), Task Force on Safer Childhood Vaccines plans within 90 days (including improving vaccine safety monitoring, transparency and research), and Attorney General support for challenges to conflicting state laws; it does not name VAERS, the Vaccine Safety Datalink or FDA, and says implementation of earlier directives has been delayed by litigation over ACIP's composition and schedule updates.

Courthouse News reports the First Circuit panel (Judges Barron, Dunlap and Kayatta) heard the government's appeal of the March 2026 order (the court had calendared argument for the next available date by an order of 2026-08-19); the Justice Department argued the plaintiffs lack standing because no reviewable final agency action is challenged, plaintiffs urged the order be upheld, and the panel gave no indication of when it would rule.

title: Move CDC vaccine safety systems to FDA and make CDC vaccine guidance non-prescriptive
uncertainties: Stage decision (blocked kept; not_started considered). Basis: the Mandate asks for two specific steps, a transfer of vaccine safety programs to FDA and a statutory or regulatory bar on prescriptive CDC guidance, and no proposal for either exists, so on those terms the objective has not started. The administration's own route to less prescriptive CDC guidance (the 2026-01-05 schedule memo that moved several diseases to shared clinical decision-making, and the ACIP votes behind it) is the closest operative action in this domain, and that is the action the district court stayed on 2026-03-16 and that is under appeal; blocked with progress 10 records that attempted route, with match parallel marking that it differs from the Mandate's mechanism. A reader could reasonably prefer not_started, and diverged was also considered. What remains operative: the pre-2026 schedule, the May 2025 Secretary directive on COVID-19 vaccination for healthy children and pregnant women (not stayed, per the Georgetown summary, which does not say what the directive now does in practice), the reinstated Task Force (HHS, 2025-08-14), and executive orders 14407 and 14420, whose implementation EO 14420 says was delayed by the litigation. Evidence limits: the order itself was not read (CourtListener is blocked by robots.txt and no copy of the order was located); the scope above comes from the plaintiffs' First Circuit filing of 2026-06-15, a Georgetown summary, a trade publication citing NPR and IDSA, and a history-of-vaccines article (2026-06-03). Sources disagree on labels: the filings call it a stay and preliminary relief, Courthouse News and the history-of-vaccines article call it an injunction; the legal basis (APA section 705 or Rule 65) was not stated in any source read. The history-of-vaccines article reports the stay of 'all 2025 votes', the plaintiffs describe votes by members appointed on three dates, and the Georgetown summary names three votes; the thirteen-member figure comes from the plaintiffs' filing (the Georgetown summary refers to 15 current members). The plaintiffs' filing says an ACIP charter re-establishment notice was published in the Federal Register on 2026-05-19 and another article reports April 2026; the dates conflict and the charter is not used in the status. The 2026-01-05 memo itself could not be read; the 17-to-11 figure rests on KFF. The First Circuit argument date of 2026-10-06 is supported by the Courthouse News report and the defendants' 2026-09-03 motion. A search for any transfer of VAERS, the Vaccine Safety Datalink or CISA to FDA in 2026 returned only 2025 reporting on a proposed VAERS overhaul and disputes over data access; the Federal Register API queries of the earlier pass found no transfer. No news of a new ACIP slate, a new ACIP meeting or Task Force plans after August 2026 was found.
